title: Location Tracking via GPS Data
description: Continuous GPS position data transmitted from the wearable device could be used to track the user's movements over time, potentially revealing sensitive patterns such as home location, workplace, frequent routes, and places of interest. This tracking could be exploited to infer the user's identity, habits, and associations.

title: User Identification from Sensor Telemetry
description: The combination of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps creates a unique biometric and behavioral fingerprint that could be used to identify the user, especially if this data is shared with third parties or analyzed in aggregate with other datasets.

title: Unauthorized Data Storage and Access
description: The wearable device (P1) receives and processes sensitive health and location data. If the device stores this data without adequate security controls, or if it shares the data with third parties without proper consent, it could lead to unauthorized disclosure of the user's private information.

title: Voluntary Data Sharing Leading to Identification
description: The user (EE1) voluntarily shares continuous sensor telemetry data with the wearable device. This act of sharing creates a privacy risk as the data contains personally identifiable information that could be used to identify the user, especially if the data is later accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Interception of GPS traces and device ID during transmission
description: GPS traces and device ID transmitted between wearable device and companion app could be intercepted by third parties during transit, enabling identification and tracking of the user's location and movements

title: Wearable device shares data that can be linked across contexts
description: The wearable device shares GPS traces and device ID that can be used to link the user's activities across different time periods and locations, creating a comprehensive movement profile

title: Companion app may disclose sensitive location data
description: The companion mobile app may store or share GPS traces and device ID with third parties without user consent, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive location information

title: Companion app may collect more data than necessary
description: The companion app may collect and store more data than necessary for the intended purpose, including detailed GPS traces and device ID, violating data minimization principles

title: Identification of User through Health Data
description: Manual logging of calorie intake, meals, and weight entries could be used to identify the user, especially if combined with other data sources or metadata.

title: Linkability of User Data
description: The manually entered health data could be linked to the user's identity or other data sources, potentially revealing patterns about the user's lifestyle, health conditions, or behaviors.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Data
description: The companion mobile app could store or process the health data in a way that exposes it to unauthorized parties, violating user privacy expectations.

title: Unintended Use of Health Data
description: The health data collected could be used for purposes beyond the user's original intent, such as marketing, insurance underwriting, or third-party sharing without explicit consent.

title: Data Manipulation in Transit
description: The manually entered data could be altered or tampered with during transmission between the user and the companion app, compromising data integrity.

title: Health Log Data Interception in Transit
description: Health log data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) transmitted from the Companion Mobile App to the Health Log Store could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing sensitive personal health information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without adequate encryption or over an unsecured network channel.

title: Linkability of Health Log Data in Transit
description: Metadata or patterns in health log data transmitted between the app and store could be used to link data records to specific individuals, enabling correlation of health behaviors across time or with other data sources.
assumptions: Data contains identifiable patterns or metadata that can be correlated with user identity.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Stored Health Logs
description: The Health Log Store may store health data in a manner that allows unauthorized access or disclosure, potentially exposing sensitive personal health information to third parties or through data breaches.
assumptions: Health log store lacks adequate access controls, encryption at rest, or proper authorization mechanisms.

title: Unawareness of Data Processing at Destination
description: Users may be unaware of how their health log data is processed, stored, or potentially shared by the Health Log Store, including any third-party access or data retention policies.
assumptions: Users lack transparency about data handling practices at the destination element.

title: Identification at Source During Data Sharing
description: The Companion Mobile App's act of sharing health log data may expose identifying information about the user at the source, particularly if the app does not properly anonymize or pseudonymize data before transmission.
assumptions: App shares data without adequate de-identification measures.

title: Identification through Location Data Sharing
description: The mobile app shares precise GPS location traces with timestamps, which can be used to identify the user based on their movement patterns and location history.

title: Linkability of Location Data in Transit
description: Location data with timestamps in transit can be linked to identify individuals and correlate their movements across different time periods.

title: Data Disclosure through Location History Storage
description: The location history store may expose stored location data to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data breaches.

title: Unintended Consequences from Location Data Storage
description: Stored location history may be used for purposes beyond the user's original intent, such as profiling, marketing, or surveillance.

title: Identification through health log analysis
description: The combination of calorie, weight, and exercise data across multiple sessions could be used to uniquely identify an individual, even without explicit identifiers like name or ID. Health patterns are personally identifiable.

title: Linkability of health data with other personal information
description: Health log data could be linked with other personal data sources (e.g., location data, purchase history, social media) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals, potentially revealing sensitive health conditions or behaviors.

title: Inadequate protection of health data at analytics service
description: The health analytics service may not adequately protect the sensitive health data it receives, potentially exposing it to unauthorized access, breaches, or improper retention.

title: Inadequate protection of health data at source
description: The health log store may share data without adequate protection mechanisms, potentially exposing sensitive information before it reaches the analytics service.

title: Linkability of Location Data in Transit
description: Location history data transferred between datastore and analytics service could be intercepted or monitored, enabling linkage of movement patterns across sessions to identify individuals or correlate with other data sources.

title: Identification via Location Patterns
description: Location data in transit contains movement patterns that could be used to identify specific individuals based on their daily routines and habitual locations.

title: Identification of Individuals from Routine Analysis
description: The health analytics service processes location history to derive daily routines and movement patterns, which could uniquely identify individuals even when direct identifiers are removed.

title: User Unawareness of Location Pattern Analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their location history is being analyzed across sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns, violating informed consent principles.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Movement Patterns
description: Derived movement patterns and daily routine information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties or used for purposes beyond the original intent of the analytics service.

title: Linkability at Source of Location History
description: The act of sharing location history from the datastore enables linkage of data across different sessions and time periods, potentially revealing sensitive information about user behavior.

title: Identifiability of inferred health insights
description: The Health Analytics Service shares inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags that could potentially identify specific individuals when combined with other data sources.

title: Unintended disclosure of sensitive health data
description: The source element shares sensitive health-related inferred insights that may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if proper access controls are not enforced at the point of sharing.

title: Linkability of health data in transit
description: Data in transit between the Health Analytics Service and Companion Mobile App could be linked with other data sources to identify individuals, especially given the sensitive nature of health-condition risk indicators.

title: Unauthorized access to health insights at destination
description: The Companion Mobile App may store or process the received health insights in ways that expose them to unauthorized access or improper retention.

title: Usurpation of health data by third parties
description: The Companion Mobile App could potentially share or misuse the received health insights with third parties without proper consent or authorization.

title: Health Condition Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The user may inadvertently reveal sensitive health information (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) to others through the app dashboard display, potentially exposing their medical condition to unintended observers.

title: Health Status Identification
description: The displayed condition indicators could allow third parties to identify the user's specific health status or medical condition, leading to potential discrimination or stigma.

title: Inaccurate Health Indicator Interpretation
description: The inferred condition indicators may be inaccurate or misleading, causing the user to make incorrect health decisions or experience unnecessary anxiety based on flawed data interpretation.

title: Regulatory Compliance Concerns
description: Displaying inferred health risk signals may raise regulatory compliance issues related to health data protection laws and informed consent requirements.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Health data, models, and location datasets transmitted to the cloud provider could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially leading to identification of individuals through the sensitive health and location information.

title: Metadata Exposure in Transit
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., source/destination identifiers, data types, transmission patterns) could be used to link or identify individuals, even if the data itself is encrypted.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure by Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider may mishandle, leak, or disclose the full health and location dataset to unauthorized third parties, violating patient privacy and data protection requirements.

title: Identification by Cloud Provider Personnel
description: Cloud provider employees or contractors with access to the hosted health data could identify individuals through the full health and location dataset, potentially leading to unauthorized profiling or surveillance.

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The cloud provider may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) regarding health data storage, access controls, and data protection measures, creating legal and privacy risks.

title: Inappropriate Data Sharing by Health Analytics Service
description: The health analytics service may share the full health and location dataset with the cloud provider without adequate consent, minimization, or purpose limitation, exposing individuals to unnecessary privacy risks.
